reviews.title: Great
reviews.comment: I bought this for mixng and mastering and got surprised. The high and low end on this headphones is just great to make critical decisions. The mids are good enough, not perfect, but still good. The soundstage and crystal clear detail on this ones, I would say is comparable to much more expensive headphones. For studio usage, there isn't a better deal for this price. Actually, I personally could stand this headphones aside the Sennheiser HD 650 (aprox 400 USD). These both sound different, but feel on a very similar level of accuracy. Really great purchase.
reviews.author: Andre Gaviria

reviews.title: revealing and very clear
reviews.comment: I wanted something light and plasticky to stand at my deck and drink with and bonus these are comfortable. My first open backs last phones were 1980's $40 Sony. These don't really add any magic to the sound or immerse you in any fairy land but they give good detail. Some stupid song with good recording quality might shine and a better song might flop so you just click next on the Spotify no problem. I splurged for the ToppingDX3pro+ and feel bad for you if you don't. I refuse to unplug the headphones to try just onmy laptop alone  once. Bass is pretty slim but I got the linear power supply and yep it improved a lot.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Clean, neutral sound and lightweight
reviews.comment: Classic Sennheiser with neutral sound and a slight roll off to the bass. This one sounds a tad brighter than the HD 600 but the bass reproduction is better. I found the mids to be more detailed and exciting as compared to its older sibling, but the treble can get a bit harsh on occasion. You can fix this with -2db at around 4khz with an EQ. Otherwise, it's hard to beat for the price! Fit can be a little tight, but it loosens over time. The headset is very light so you won't feel it on your head after a while.
